function: above_phy, p. 7: the DRL agent (H-DSAC) learns UAV trajectories, user-UAV and UAV-satellite pairings, the final aggregation satellite and FL aggregation weights; transmit powers and bandwidths are fixed and FL aggregation is digital.
notes: Excluded as above_phy. p. 7: the problem optimizes "1) the trajectory of each UAV; 2) the pairing between UAVs and users (uplink); 3) the pairing between UAVs and satellites (uplink); 4) the selection of the final aggregation satellite, 5) the pairing between satellites and UAVs (downlink)" and "6)-8)" the edge, cloud and final aggregation weights. The DRL action (p. 8, Eq. 16) contains only these variables. They are UAV trajectory, user association and access, and FL-level decisions; no transmit power, bandwidth or beam is learned. Ground, UAV and LEO transmit powers are fixed at 0.1 W, 1 W and 2 W, and the bandwidth is 10 MHz (p. 10). The "resource allocation" of the title refers to these pairings and weights. The FL aggregation is digital: local models are uploaded at the link rate (Eq. 2) and averaged at the UAVs and satellites (Eqs. 11-13, pp. 5-6). It would therefore also fall outside area 7 under check 5. Checks 1 to 3 pass: research article whose method is a learned DRL agent. The PDF (arXiv 2408.02501v1) matches the DOI: same title and authors as the Crossref record.
